text: The vector $\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ is rotated through a right angle, passing through the y-axis in its way and the resulting vector is $\vec{b}$. Then the projection of $3\vec{a}+\sqrt{2}\vec{b}$ on $\vec{c}=5\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Rotating $⃗{a}$ through a right angle so that it passes through the y-axis keeps $⃗{b}$ in the plane of $⃗{a}$ and $\hat{j}$, with $⃗{b}⟂⃗{a}$ and $|⃗{b}|=|⃗{a}|=\sqrt{6}$. So $⃗{b}=λ⃗{a}+μ\hat{j}$.

$⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{a}=0\Rightarrow 6λ+2μ=0\Rightarrow μ=-3λ$

$⃗{b}=λ(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})-3λ\hat{j}=λ(-\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})$

$|⃗{b}|=\sqrt{3}|λ|=\sqrt{6}\Rightarrow |λ|=\sqrt{2}$.

$⃗{a}$ makes an angle $α$ with the y-axis where $\cos α=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}}$, so $α<90^{\circ }$; after crossing the y-axis, $⃗{b}$ makes the angle $90^{\circ }-α$ with it, which is acute. Hence $⃗{b}\cdot \hat{j}=-λ>0$, so $λ=-\sqrt{2}$:

$⃗{b}=\sqrt{2}\hat{i}+\sqrt{2}\hat{j}-\sqrt{2}\hat{k}$

$3⃗{a}+\sqrt{2}⃗{b}=(-3\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=-\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

The projection on $⃗{c}$ is

$\frac{(-\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+\hat{k})\cdot (5\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k})}{|⃗{c}|}=\frac{-5+32+3}{\sqrt{50}}=\frac{30}{5\sqrt{2}}=3\sqrt{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text: The minimum value of the function $f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{2}e^{|x-t|}dt$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $0\leq x\leq 2$, split the integral at $t=x$:

$f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}e^{x-t}dt+\int\limits _{x}^{2}e^{t-x}dt=(e^{x}-1)+(e^{2-x}-1)=e^{x}+e^{2-x}-2$

By AM–GM, $e^{x}+e^{2-x}\geq 2\sqrt{e^{x}\cdot e^{2-x}}=2e$, with equality at $x=1$, so the least value on $[0,2]$ is $2e-2=2(e-1)$.

For $x>2$, $f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{2}e^{x-t}dt=e^{x-2}(e^{2}-1)>e^{2}-1$.

For $x<0$, $f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{2}e^{t-x}dt=e^{-x}(e^{2}-1)>e^{2}-1$.

Since $e^{2}-1=(e-1)(e+1)>2(e-1)$, the minimum value of $f$ is $2(e-1)$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text: The mean and variance of the marks obtained by the students in a test are 10 and 4 respectively. Later, the marks of one of the students is increased from 8 to 12. If the new mean of the marks is 10.2, then their new variance is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $N$ be the number of students. Raising one mark from 8 to 12 increases the total by 4, so the mean increases by $\dfrac{4}{N}$:

$10+\dfrac{4}{N}=10.2\Rightarrow N=20$

The original variance gives $\dfrac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{20}-10^{2}=4$, so $\sum x_{i}^{2}=20\times 104=2080$.

After the change, $\sum x_{i}^{2}=2080-8^{2}+12^{2}=2080-64+144=2160$.

$σ_{\text{new}}^{2}=\dfrac{2160}{20}-(10.2)^{2}=108-104.04=3.96$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text: The points of intersection of the line $ax+by=0,(a\neq b)$ and the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-2x=0$ are $A(α,0)$ and $B(1,β)$. The image of the circle with AB as a diameter in the line $x+y+2=0$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The line $ax+by=0$ passes through the origin, and the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-2x=0$ has centre $(1,0)$ and radius 1.

$B(1,β)$ lies on the circle: $1+β^{2}-2=0\Rightarrow β=\pm 1$. It lies on the line: $a+bβ=0\Rightarrow a=-bβ$. For $β=-1$ this gives $a=b$, which is excluded, so $β=1$, $a=-b$ and the line is $y=x$.

$A(α,0)$ lies on $y=x$, so $α=0$. Hence $A(0,0)$ and $B(1,1)$.

The circle on $AB$ as diameter has centre $\left (\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$ and radius $\dfrac{AB}{2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

The image of the centre in $x+y+2=0$ is given by

$\frac{x-\frac{1}{2}}{1}=\frac{y-\frac{1}{2}}{1}=\frac{-2\left (\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}+2\right )}{1^{2}+1^{2}}=-3\Rightarrow \left (-\frac{5}{2},-\frac{5}{2}\right ).$

The image circle has the same radius:

$\left (x+\frac{5}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (y+\frac{5}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}+5x+5y+\frac{25}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}+5x+5y+12=0$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

$ax+2ay-3az=1$

has unique solution and infinitely many solutions. Then
options: $\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{S}_{1})=2$ and S${}_{2}$ is an infinite set
S${}_{1}$ is an infinite set and n(S${}_{2}$) = 2
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The coefficient determinant is

$D=\left |\begin{array}{lll} a & 2a & -3a \\ 2a+1 & 2a+3 & a+1 \\ 3a+5 & a+5 & a+2 \end{array}\right |=a\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2a+1 & 2a+3 & a+1 \\ 3a+5 & a+5 & a+2 \end{array}\right |.$

Applying $C_{2}\to C_{2}-2C_{1}$ and $C_{3}\to C_{3}+3C_{1}$:

$D=a\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2a+1 & 1-2a & 7a+4 \\ 3a+5 & -5a-5 & 10a+17 \end{array}\right |=a[(1-2a)(10a+17)+(7a+4)(5a+5)].$

Here $(1-2a)(10a+17)=-20a^{2}-24a+17$ and $(7a+4)(5a+5)=35a^{2}+55a+20$, so $D=a\left (15a^{2}+31a+37\right )$.

The quadratic $15a^{2}+31a+37$ has discriminant $31^{2}-4(15)(37)=961-2220<0$, so it is never zero, and $D\neq 0$ for every $a\neq 0$.

The system therefore has a unique solution for every $a\in \mathrm{ℝ}-\{0\}$, so $S_{1}=\mathrm{ℝ}-\{0\}$ and $S_{2}=\Phi$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Let S = {1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11}. The number of non-empty subsets of S that have the sum of all elements a multiple of 3, is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By remainder on division by $3$, the elements of S fall into three classes: remainder $0$: $\{3\}$; remainder $1$: $\{1,7,10\}$; remainder $2$: $\{2,5,11\}$.

A subset with $p$ elements of remainder $1$ and $q$ elements of remainder $2$ has sum a multiple of $3$ exactly when $p+2q\equiv 0(\mathrm{mod}3)$, i.e. $p\equiv q(\mathrm{mod}3)$; the element $3$ does not affect this.

With $0\leq p,q\leq 3$, the possible pairs are $(0,0)$, $(1,1)$, $(2,2)$, $(3,3)$, $(3,0)$ (the set $\{1,7,10\}$) and $(0,3)$ (the set $\{2,5,11\}$). The number of ways of choosing these elements is

$1+{}^{3}C_{1}\times {}^{3}C_{1}+{}^{3}C_{2}\times {}^{3}C_{2}+1+1+1=1+9+9+1+1+1=22$

Each of these $22$ choices can be taken with or without the element $3$, giving $2\times 22=44$ subsets, one of which is the empty set.

Number of non-empty subsets $=44-1=43$.

Hence, the answer is 43.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text: Let $x$ and $y$ be distinct integers where $1\leq x\leq 25$ and $1\leq y\leq 25$. Then, the number of ways of choosing $x$ and $y$, such that $x+y$ is divisible by 5, is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $x+y=5λ$

Possible cases are

$\begin{array}{lll} x & y & \text{Number of ways} \\ 5λ(5,10,15,20,25) & 5λ(5,10,15,20,25) & 20 \\ 5λ+1(1,6,11,16,21) & 5λ+4(4,9,14,19,24) & 25 \\ 5λ+2(2,7,12,17,22) & 5λ+3(3,8,13,18,23) & 25 \\ 5λ+3(3,8,13,18,23) & 5λ+2(2,7,12,17,22) & 25 \\ 5λ+4(4,9,14,19,24) & 5λ+1(1,6,11,16,21) & 25 \end{array}$

Total number of ways $=20+25+25+25+25=120$

Note : In first case total number of ways = 20 as in the question given that the chosen $x$ and $y$ are distinct integers each time. So when you choose x as 5 then you can't choose y as 5. Possible values of y are (10, 15, 20, 25). So, here four possible pairs of (x, y) possible { (5, 10), (5, 15), (5, 20), (5, 25)}.

Similarly, four possible pairs of (x, y) possible each time when x = 10, 15, 20 and 25.

$\therefore$ Total number of ways in the first case = 5 $\times$ 4 = 20.

$\begin{array}{lllllll} b=A+8d+1 \\  \\ c=A+16d+2 \\  \\ \left |\begin{array}{lll} a & 7 & 1 \\ 2b & 17 & 1 \\ c & 17 & 1 \end{array}\right |=-70 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} A+6d & 7 & 1 \\ 2A+16d+2 & 17 & 1 \\ A+16d+2 & 17 & 1 \end{array}\right |=-70 \\  \\ R_{3}\to R_{3}-R_{2},R_{2}\to R_{2}-R_{1} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} A+6d & 7 & 1 \\ A+10d+2 & 10 & 0 \\ -A & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right |=-70 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow \quad  & A=-7 \\  \\ \qquad a=A+6d=29\Rightarrow d=6 \\  \\ \qquad b=-7+48+1=42 \\  \\ \qquad c=-7+96+2=91 \\  \\ \qquad c-a-b=91-29-42=20 \\  \\ \qquad \text{Sum}=\dfrac{20}{2}\left [2\times 20+19\times \dfrac{6}{12}\right ]=10\left [40+\dfrac{19}{2}\right ]=495 \end{array}$

text: If the area enclosed by the parabolas $\mathrm{P}_{1}:2\mathrm{y}=5\mathrm{x}^{2}$ and $\mathrm{P}_{2}:\mathrm{x}^{2}-\mathrm{y}+6=0$ is equal to the area enclosed by $\mathrm{P}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{y}=α\mathrm{x},α>0$, then $α^{3}$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2}+6=\frac{5}{2}x^{2}\Rightarrow x=\pm 2$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Area between}P_{1}\text{and}P_{2}\text{[Say}A_{1}] \\  \\ =\int\limits _{-2}^{2}\left (x^{2}+6\right )-\dfrac{5}{2}x^{2}dx \\  \\ =2\int\limits _{0}^{2}\left (6-\dfrac{3}{2}x^{2}\right )dx=2\left [6x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{2}\right ]_{0}^{2}=16 \end{array}$

$\left. \begin{array}{l} ax=\dfrac{5}{2}x^{2}\Rightarrow x=0,\dfrac{2a}{5} \\  \\ \text{Area between}P_{1}\text{and}y=ax\text{[Say}A_{2}\text{]} \\  \\ =\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{2α}{5}}ax-\dfrac{5}{2}x^{2}dx \\  \\ =\dfrac{ax^{2}}{2}-\dfrac{5}{6}x^{3}\right ]_{0}^{\frac{2a}{5}}:\dfrac{2a^{3}}{75} \\  \\ A_{1}=A_{2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{2a^{3}}{75}=16 \\  \\ a^{3}=600 \end{array}$

text: If the sum of all the solutions of $\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{2x}{1-x^{2}}\right )+\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{1-x^{2}}{2x}\right )=\frac{π}{3},-1<x<1,x\neq 0$, is $α-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}$, then $α$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $-1<x<1$, $\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{2x}{1-x^{2}}\right )=2\tan ^{-1}x$.

For $x>0$, $\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{2x}>0$, so $\cot ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{2x}\right )=\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{2x}{1-x^{2}}\right )=2\tan ^{-1}x$. For $x<0$, $\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{2x}<0$, so $\cot ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{2x}\right )=π+\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{2x}{1-x^{2}}\right )=π+2\tan ^{-1}x$.

Case $0<x<1$: $4\tan ^{-1}x=\dfrac{π}{3}\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}x=\dfrac{π}{12}\Rightarrow x=\tan 15^{\circ }=2-\sqrt{3}$, which lies in $(0,1)$.

Case $-1<x<0$: $π+4\tan ^{-1}x=\dfrac{π}{3}\Rightarrow 4\tan ^{-1}x=-\dfrac{2π}{3}\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}x=-\dfrac{π}{6}\Rightarrow x=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, which lies in $(-1,0)$.

The sum of the solutions is

$2-\sqrt{3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=2-\frac{3+1}{\sqrt{3}}=2-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}},$

so $α=2$.

Hence, the answer is 2.
